lout

LOUT (rhymes with 'shout') · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Lout is a rough, clumsy, ill-mannered man or boy.

The wedding photographer warned the groomsmen to behave, worried that one loud lout among them might ruin the formal photos.

Example

A pair of louts cut in line at the amusement park, shoving past a family with small children without a hint of apology.

Lout usually describes rowdy, physically careless behavior in a group or public setting -- shoving, shouting, cutting in line -- rather than a quiet or private kind of rudeness.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

hooligan: A hooligan is a rowdy troublemaker who runs with a crowd -- smashing seats, brawling in the stands, wrecking things at matches and concerts. A lout is rough and ill-mannered too, but a lout acts alone as often as not, and his offense is crude carelessness rather than deliberate destruction.

brute: A brute is defined by violence and cruelty -- force is the whole idea of the word. A lout is not necessarily violent at all: louts shove past you and barge through doorways out of sheer crude carelessness, not out of any wish to hurt anyone.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

gentleman: a polite, considerate man

gallant: chivalrous and courteous

Where it sits · how physically rough the behavior gets

boor → lout → ruffian

boor vs. lout: A boor (also in this unit) sits a step below a lout: rude and socially clumsy company, but not necessarily rough or physical the way a lout is.

ruffian vs. lout: A ruffian goes further than a lout, adding real physical menace or violence.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — lout: possibly from an old word meaning 'to bow or stoop' (Middle English, origin uncertain)

Put it together: Lout's exact history is uncertain -- it may come from an old word meaning 'to stoop or bow low,' which would fit an oafish figure who slouches and shows no polish. Whatever its origin, by the 1500s it had settled into its modern meaning: a clumsy, ill-mannered man or boy.

Use the root in a new word: loutish: Loutish simply means 'behaving like a lout' -- rowdy, rough, and without manners.

Word Choice

Lout leans rougher and more physical than its cousin boor (also in this unit) -- picture rowdy shoving in a crowd rather than just bad table manners.
